chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who goes out on a journey and his wife is with him, can he wash her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and (he can wash) his mother and his sister and similar to this, a cloth is cast upon her private part.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband wash his wife's body if she dies during a journey?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of a husband washing his wife’s body during travel, extending the ruling to her mother and sister. It specifies the modesty requirement of covering the *awrah* with a cloth, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community regarding ritual purity (*ghusl*) in domestic and travel contexts.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man going out in a journey and with him is his wife, can he wash her (if she were to die)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and (he can wash) his mother, and his sister and such as this, casting a cloth upon her private part’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who goes on a journey with his wife (and she dies), can he give her Ghusl (bath)? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so and so also is the case of his mother and sister. Such person’s private parts are covered with a piece of cloth.’”
